title.narrative: 1. Reduce corruption in ports and encourage further investments and initiatives to address integrity challenges in ports in Africa 2. Increased global level of awareness and engagement of governments, donors and the private sector about integrity challenges in ports
1.a Level of corruption in ports in Nigeria

actual.value: 1.a Corrupt practices in ports in Nigeria decreased. Launched in 2019, the MACN HelpDesk is a crucial tool in combating corruption in Nigerian ports, enabling private sector members to report corrupt demands and achieve swift grievance resolutions. Its usage has grown significantly, from 6 members in 2019 to 41 by the end of 2023, a 583% increase. By the end of 2023, 1017 Pre-Arrival Notifications (PANs) were registered, with 143 incidents of corruption escalated. Of these, 136 were resolved by the Nigerian Shippers Council and other authorities, maintaining a 95% resolution rate. The anonymous incident reporting system saw a decrease in reported incidents from 266 in 2019 to 54 by 2023, an 80% reduction. The HelpDesk impact extends beyond just reporting. It has significantly cut case resolution times from 7-8 days to an average of 8 hours. This efficiency translates to significant reduction in operational costs from $150,000 to $20,000 or less per vessel. Therefore, the HelpDesk, along with other mechanisms, has empowered the private sector and reduced operational costs for vessels, including port dues, fuel, security, and hire costs.

title.narrative: 1. Reduce corruption in ports and encourage further investments and initiatives to address integrity challenges in ports in Africa 2. Increased global level of awareness and engagement of governments, donors and the private sector about integrity challenges in ports
1.b New collective action initiatives

actual.value: 1.b Minimum two new collective action initiatives and possible funding opportunities explored for expansion of MACN’s integrity work in Africa. Successful models from Nigeria have been replicated in Ukraine, and similar strategies are being discussed in Ghana. MACN further went on to receive funding from the Siemens Integrity Initiative - Creating fair market conditions, Fighting corruption and fraud through Collective Action, Education & Training – Third Round for expansion of its activities in Nigeria and Danida under the Danish ‘Resource Mobilisation for Development. Anti-Corruption and Domestic Re-source Mobilisation Programme 2023 – 2026’.

title.narrative: 1. Reduce corruption in ports and encourage further investments and initiatives to address integrity challenges in ports in Africa 2. Increased global level of awareness and engagement of governments, donors and the private sector about integrity challenges in ports
2.a High-level engagement and participation in MACN’s work

actual.value: 2.a Engagement by MACN of a wide range of stakeholders in events and initiatives. The project's theory of change emphasizes multi-stakeholder engagement by offering clear, safe alternatives to corrupt practices and addressing barriers such as fear of retribution and apathy through public-private dialogue. MACN actively engaged a diverse range of stakeholders in events and initiatives, which has empowered the private sector operating in Nigeria to report corruption via the Anti Corruption Helpdesk. This engagement has led to significant reductions in port delays and corrupt demands, benefiting smaller businesses. The growth of the National Integrity Alliance, with over 270 members, highlights local demand for reform, particularly benefiting small and medium-sized businesses. Flexibility and public sector engagement, particularly during crises like the COVID-19 pandemic, have been crucial. Developing inclusive integrity data platforms has fostered greater collaboration and trust among stakeholders both public and private, ensuring the success of Collective Action initiatives in West Africa and beyond.
